name: Measurement of reactor neutrino oscillation with the first JUNO data
title: Measurement of reactor neutrino oscillation with the first JUNO data

claim.quote: Measurement of reactor neutrino oscillation with the first JUNO data

summary.plain: Using its first two months of data, JUNO measured two key numbers describing how neutrinos change type as they travel, with more precision than every earlier experiment combined.
summary.technical: First-data (59.1 days, 2025-08-26 to 2025-11-02) simultaneous precision measurement of sin²θ₁₂ = 0.3092 ± 0.0087 and Δm²₂₁ = (7.50 ± 0.12) × 10⁻⁵ eV², improving combined-world precision on these parameters by a factor of 1.6.

why_it_matters.value: Demonstrates that the JUNO detector performs at or above its sub-percent design precision within months of starting operation, and sets up its long-term programme to determine the neutrino mass ordering.
why_it_matters.quote: Achieving such precision within only two months of operation shows that JUNO is performing exactly as designed.

key_value_text.quote: $\sin^2 θ_{12} = 0.3092\,\pm\,0.0087$ and $Δm^2_{21} = (7.50\,\pm\,0.12)\times10^{-5}\;{\rm eV}^2$ for the normal mass ordering scenario, improving the precision by a factor of 1.6 relative to the combination of all previous measurements
key_value_text.note: Quote is the abstract text as shown on the arXiv abstract page (preprint of the Nature paper); the Nature abstract states the same values. Values are for the normal mass ordering scenario.

significance.note: This is a precision parameter measurement, not a discovery/observation/evidence claim with a single reported sigma; no significance figure applies.

notes: IHEP announced these results at a press conference on 2025-11-19 (src:juno-ihep-first-results-en), ahead of the 2026-06-10 Nature publication; `date`/`date_kind` here record the publication, per the ontology's `result.date_kind` field distinguishing announcement/preprint/publication.
